title: Chemicals for stone: acid etches, cleaners and sealers
audience: Stone and terrazzo restoration technicians who select, store, use and dispose of cleaners, etches, poultices and sealers
learningOutcomes: Find and read the Safety Data Sheet and product instructions before using any stone chemical
Choose a stone chemical that the manufacturer approves for the material and finish
Store and handle chemicals without mixing products unless the manufacturer allows it
Explain why a test patch comes before any acid etch or strong cleaner
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: WorkSafe Queensland, Chemical reaction exposes worker to toxic gas (no date on page; incident dated March 2022).

instruction.heading: Read before you pour
instruction.body: Stone work uses several families of product: acidic etches, alkaline and neutral cleaners, poultices and stain removers, and impregnating and topical sealers. Each product has a Safety Data Sheet, and the SDS is the first source of hazard information. Read the sections on hazards, first aid, personal protective equipment, handling, storage and incompatible materials before the product is opened on site. The label and the product's technical data sheet give the approved use and the dilution. This course does not set dilutions or contact times, because they depend on the product and the stone. Use the product only on the surfaces the manufacturer approves, and only after a test patch as set in “Pre-work surface assessment and test patches”. WorkSafe Queensland's incident alert (page undated; incident March 2022) advises checking labels and SDS for handling, storage and emergency steps, and keeping them within easy reach of workers.

instruction.heading: Storage, mixing and waste
instruction.body: Store chemicals by hazard class, away from incompatible materials, and keep the lids closed. Do not mix products unless the manufacturer's instructions say that the mixture is approved. Mixing one product with another can produce heat or gases. WorkSafe Queensland's 2022 alert describes sodium hypochlorite added to sulphuric acid, releasing toxic chlorine gas, and warns against mixing incompatible chemicals; acids must therefore never be mixed with bleach or hypochlorite products. Keep the SDS for each product on site and in a location that workers can reach in an emergency. Label any diluted solution with the product, the dilution, the date and the hazard. Follow the SDS and the site's waste procedure, and check the state environment authority before disposing of any residue into a drain or ground.

instruction.heading: Choosing the product and the test
instruction.body: Match the product to the stone and to the finish. An acid etch that suits a honed granite may dull or damage a polished marble or a terrazzo finish, and a cleaner that suits a sealed surface may strip an unsealed one. Use the manufacturer's list of approved uses first, and then test on a concealed patch as set in “Pre-work surface assessment and test patches”. Use the lowest strength and the shortest contact time that the manufacturer states and that the test patch supports. This course's teaching rule is that an acid etch used near people or pets needs a documented control plan before use.

procedure: Identify the product and find its SDS and technical data sheet before use.
Read the sections on hazards, first aid, PPE, handling, storage and incompatible materials, and note any product-specific conditions.
Confirm that the manufacturer approves the product for the stone and the finish on the job.
Set up ventilation and the PPE listed in the SDS, and keep people and pets away from the work area when an acid etch is used.
Carry out a test patch on a concealed area, and record the result before the full application.
Use the approved dilution and contact time only, and neutralise or rinse as the product instructions say.
Store the product and its residue as the SDS directs, and dispose of waste by the site procedure and state rules.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner wants to use a strong acid etch on a polished granite benchtop to remove a rust mark. The cleaner suggests mixing it with the bleach already in the van, because the bleach 'works on everything'.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner do, and what must not happen?
workedExamples.reasoning: Mixing an acid with bleach is not allowed and can release hazardous gas. The cleaner reads the SDS and the product's technical data sheet, checks that the manufacturer approves the product for polished granite, and carries out a test patch in a concealed place. If the finish or the test shows damage, the work is referred rather than forced. Ventilation and PPE from the SDS are set up before use, and the rust mark is treated only with the approved product.

equipmentAndPpe: Safety Data Sheet and technical data sheet for each product, kept on site
PPE listed in the SDS for the product (eye protection, gloves and others as the SDS requires)
Ventilation or extraction suited to the product and the work area
Labelled containers and a spill kit appropriate to the product
Test patch materials and a record sheet

commonErrors.error: Using a product without reading its SDS or technical data sheet.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the SDS and the product instructions first. The product label alone is not enough.

commonErrors.error: Mixing two cleaners to get more power.
commonErrors.prevention: Never mix products unless the manufacturer says the mixture is approved. Never mix acid with bleach or hypochlorite products.

commonErrors.error: Using an acid etch on polished marble because it worked on a granite floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the approved uses for the material and the finish, then run a test patch.

commonErrors.error: Keeping the SDS in the van only.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the SDS on site and in a place workers can reach in an emergency.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The rule that an acid etch used near people or pets needs a documented control plan is a course teaching rule. The rule is not evidence of a legal standard.

Stop-work rule: stop if the SDS is not on site, if the product is not approved for the stone and finish, if a test patch is damaged or unexpected, or if a mixture is being made that the manufacturer does not approve. Completing this lesson does not qualify any person to handle any particular product.

qualityStandard: An SDS is on site for each product in use.
The product is approved by the manufacturer for the stone and the finish.
A test patch is recorded before any acid etch or strong cleaner is applied to the full area.
No products are mixed unless the manufacturer's instructions allow it.
documentationEvidence: Product name, batch number and SDS reference for each product used
Ventilation and PPE used for the product
summary: Read the SDS and product instructions before any stone chemical is used.
Use only the product, dilution and contact time the manufacturer approves.
Never mix products unless the manufacturer allows it; never mix acid with bleach.
Test on a concealed patch before any acid etch or strong cleaner.
Store, label and dispose of chemicals as the SDS directs and as state rules require.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: WorkSafe Queensland, Chemical reaction exposes worker to toxic gas (no date on page; incident dated March 2022).

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the first step before using a stone chemical?
options: Dilute it to full strength
Read the SDS and the product instructions
Mix it with another cleaner for better results
Apply it to the client's centre piece to test it

knowledgeChecks.question: Which mixing action is correct?
options: Mix acid with bleach to increase the power of the clean on the job site
Mix any two cleaners in the same bucket to save time on the job site
Mix products only where the manufacturer says the mixture is approved
Mix products in a sealed bottle to hide the reaction from view of the client

knowledgeChecks.question: An acid etch is considered for a polished marble surface. What is the correct step?
options: Apply it across the whole surface to save time on the job site today
Skip the test because marble is a strong stone that resists acid well
Use it only at night when the site is quiet and the air is still and cool
Test first on a concealed area and check the manufacturer's approved uses

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should the SDS for a product be kept?
options: On site, where workers can reach it
Only in the office, in a drawer
With the client, in their home
In the waste bin after the job

knowledgeChecks.question: Under this course's teaching rule, what is required for an acid etch used near people or pets?
options: No control plan is needed
A documented control plan before use
Only a licensed person may use any product
The client must sign the product label
